title: fix(serve): served writes commit — the write lock is a derived artifact, not a topology violation
context:
`hunch serve` flushes inside its cross-process write lock, so `.hunch/write.lock` is always
present when `git add .` stages the record. The staged-memory backstop treated a non-JSON,
non-derived file as a violation and, on the public-store path, skipped the commit quietly:
every served write reported durability "local" and the partition repository never gained a
commit (1.26.0, 1.26.1). The lock file is now classified as a derived artifact alongside the
SQLite index and temp files. Test: a git-i
decision: Changed code in src/extractors, test/serve.test.ts (2 file(s)).
